paper_summary: Conference abstract (24th Compatibility Aging Stockpile Stewardship Conference, LANL/KCP, 2002) on replacing obsolete polymeric materials in the LANL stockpile. One of its three sections concerns the high-temperature syntactic foam used as the W76 aft support: carbon microballoons (CMB) in a polyimide binder (Kerimid 601, discontinued because of MDA) replaced by an APO-BMI binder, with thermally activated (TA) CMB and removal of the Thornel carbon mat. Table 1 compares flexural and compressive properties of the 1977 baseline material, stockpile returns, and new 40/60 APO-BMI billets, and concludes that comparable flexural properties are obtained without Thornel mat and without sacrificing compressive properties.

extraction_notes: This is a scanned 2002 conference abstract; the OCR of Table 1 is severely degraded. The column headings and all row/column alignment are lost - only a loose stream of numbers survives: strength/modulus-scale values 571, 587, 480, 670, 552+/-48, 897+/-17, 878+/-21, 553+/-22, 735+/-62, 648+/-44; strength-scale values 7.93, 7.51, 5.93+/-0.36, 7.52+/-0.35, 7.51+/-0.40; strain values 0.94, 1.46, 0.53+/-0.04, 0.46+/-0.02, 0.56+/-0.02; plus orphan fragments '76' and '9.'. The surviving row labels are 'Flexural Strength, MPa', 'Modulus, MPa', 'Flexural Strain (%)' and 'Compressive Strength, MPa'. Because two distinct hundreds-of-MPa groups survive but only one modulus label, it cannot be determined which numbers are flexural modulus, which are compressive modulus/strength, and which are flexural strength; those values were therefore left null rather than guessed. Only the strain row is unambiguous by magnitude (the only sub-unity values with a '(%)' label), so strain_at_failure is the only property extracted, converted from percent to fraction. The paper says the table has 8 columns; the five surviving value groups were mapped as columns 1-2 (McIlroy 1977, Kerimid 601, secondary data) and columns 6-8 (as-received CMB, TA CMB, inner support billet, all APO-BMI), based on the text's statement that thermal activation increased the flexural properties (the three +/- columns rise from the first to the second value in every row). Columns 3, 4 and 5 (including the stockpile-return averages) produced no recoverable numbers. Particle loading was left null: the '40/60' and '40/60/5' designations are stated but the paper never says whether the numbers are weight or volume percent, nor which of columns 1/2 is which formulation. Test temperature, standard, density and particle geometry are not reported. All confidences are low; this extraction should be re-done from the original PDF/report if precise values are needed.
